blocks.text: This document summarizes the transition of the Medical Screening Assistant from a prototype to a secure, local AI-powered system.
The system has been refactored to eliminate client-side trust and implement a strict 'Server-Side State' model.

items: Session Opacity: The client now only holds a random session ID. All facts and status are managed in server memory.
Secure Prolog Bridge: Switched from string interpolation to a JSON-based stdin/stdout interface for SWI-Prolog.
Allowlist Validation: Every input to the Prolog engine is validated against a hardcoded allowlist of approved symptoms and diseases.
Local AI Integration: Implemented a validated extraction layer using the gemma4:12b-mlx model via Ollama.
Deterministic Emergency Triage: A high-priority safety layer now runs before any diagnosis, immediately escalating severe symptoms (e.g., crushing chest pain) to emergency services.
Conservative Fallback: Implemented a regex-based extraction fallback that ensures the system remains functional if the LLM is unavailable, while strictly avoiding false positives.
Input Sanitization: Fixed regex boundary escapes to prevent misclassification of negative answers.
Injection Resistance: Verified that malicious Prolog payloads cannot penetrate the validated JSON bridge.
Non-Diagnostic Branding: Renamed the tool to 'Medical Screening Assistant' and updated all output to refer to 'screening results' rather than 'diagnoses'.
Ranked Screening: The system now returns a ranked list of all potential matches above a threshold, rather than a single first-match result.
Safe Rendering: Updated the UI to use DOM APIs instead of innerHTML, preventing XSS from model-generated content.

blocks.text: The refactor was verified using strict Test-Driven Development (TDD):

items: Unit Tests: 31 tests passed, covering negation, session isolation, and triage logic.
Integration: Confirmed end-to-end flow from /start to final screening results.
Security Audit: Verified immunity to session forgery and Prolog injection.
